title: WW3-SWRT: WAVEWATCH III 7.14 with the sparse Webb-Resio-Tracy (SWRT) nonlinear source term
description:
WAVEWATCH III (version 7.14) with the sparse Webb–Resio–Tracy (SWRT) source term for the nonlinear four-wave interaction, selected by the switch NL6. SWRT retains K mirror-image pairs of configurations of the WRT integration space, each with an optimized gain; the operator of the paper has K = 36.

The archive contains the model source (SWRT in model/src/w3snl6md.F90), the switch file, the K = 36 operator, and the namelists and scripts of the 1° global simulation of the paper. The large restart and ERA5 wind inputs of the test are not included.

Since v1.1, the archive also holds the scripts that make the operator for another spectral grid (tools/): WRT's quadrature for the grid, the table of its rows, synthetic practice spectra, the selection of the configurations and their gains, and checks against WRT. For the paper's grid they reproduced the K = 30 operator of v1.1 exactly. v1.1 also adds the Xnl source files of WRT (NL2), which v1.0 lacked.

v1.2 adds the setups of the six single-point simulations of the paper (single_point/), with a patch that restores the semi-implicit source-term integration and the standard DIA used in them, and the SWRT operators for all other K of the paper (inputs/operators/). Built with the patch, the v1.2 code reproduced the paper's single-point runs with WRT and DIA bit for bit, and those with SWRT to within 1e-6.

v1.3 replaces the operators by the paper's SWRT, K = 36 configurations on 18 offsets (inputs/swrt_K36.ww3op), selected by the search of the paper under a limit on the offsets, with random restarts (now in tools/build_swrt.py, which reproduces the paper's selection). The kernel groups the rows by resonance curve, so that the rows of one offset share their work, and S_nl is computed at all frequencies of the grid. v1.3 also adds three configuration sets of the hybrid in the paper's Discussion, with the rule that assigns a spectrum to one of them (inputs/hybrid/). The operators of v1.2 for other K are not included. Built with the patch of single_point/, the archived code reproduces the paper's single-point runs with SWRT bit for bit in four of the six scenarios and to within 1e-6 of the largest spectral density in the other two.

v1.4 matches the current version of the paper. Only the hybrid (inputs/hybrid/) changes: opposing seas are found from the f⁴-weighted directional distribution, and the sets for broad seas and for opposing seas are those selected under this rule. The model code and the SWRT operator are those of v1.3.
